lesson: Today we work on one thing, the line break. A line break is the place where a line stops and your eye or your breath drops to the next line. The poet chooses that spot. Sometimes the sentence keeps going, so the break holds you for a beat before the next word arrives. Watch three spots. The way he keeps, no ledger but the morning. The line stops after keeps, so for one beat you don't know what he keeps. Then no ledger lands. Same with the frost is on the rail. You wait a beat for the rail. And the barn stands, waiting its turn. You hold on stands, then get waiting. This works because the pause makes you expect something. The held word arrives a little harder. Try this, break a line one word before the point, so the listener waits for it. The second time, listen for how so up, snaps shut after all those held breaths. The third time, listen for how so up, snaps shut after all those held breaths. The third time, listen for how so up, snaps shut after all those held breaths.
